author: Harabedian (D)

title: Reproductive Health Emergency Preparedness Program
summary: Establishes the Reproductive Health Emergency Preparedness Program for the purpose of expanding and improving access to reproductive and sexual health care in emergency departments across the State. Requires the Department of Health Care Access and Information to award the grants and administer the RHEPP. Requires the department to establish minimum standards, funding schedules, and procedures for awarding grants. Limits the permissible uses of grant funds.
author: Krell (D)

title: Food Delivery Platforms: Customer Service
summary: Requires a food delivery platform to provide a full refund to the customer if an order is not delivered or the wrong order is delivered, unless the food delivery platform determines that the customer was responsible for the nondelivery or finds evidence indicating the refund request may be fraudulent. Requires the food delivery platform to refund the amount of the original paid gratuity to the customer but to not take or deduct the original gratuity amount from the delivery driver.
author: Bauer-Kahan (D)

title: Deepfake Pornography
summary: Provides that existing law grants to a depicted individual a cause of action against a person who creates and intentionally discloses sexually explicit material. Grants to a depicted individual a cause of action against a person who knows, or reasonably should know, that the depicted individual was a minor when the digitized sexually explicit material was created. Grants a cause of action to that depicted individual against a person who knowingly facilitates or recklessly aids or abets prohibited conduct.
author: Bauer-Kahan (D)

title: Health Care Coverage Reporting
summary: Requires a health care service plan or health insurer that imposes prior authorization to report specified prior authorization data from the previous calendar year on its internet website on or before February 1, 2026, for health care service plans, on or before February 1, 2028, for health insurers, and annually on or before February 1 thereafter. Requires a health care service plan or health insurer to annually report specified claims and prior authorization data to the relevant department.
author: Ortega (D)

title: Real Estate: Digitally Altered Images: Disclosure
topics: Deepfake; Housing; Notification; Private Sector Use; Provenance
summary: Requires a real estate broker or salesperson, or person acting on their behalf, who includes a digitally altered image in an advertisement or other promotional material for the sale of real property to include a specified disclosure. Requires, if the advertisement or promotional material is posted on an internet website, the same image without digital alteration to be included.
author: Pellerin (D)

title: Health Care: Legally Protected Health Care Activity
summary: Expands the Address Confidentiality Program to a gender-affirming health care provider, employee or volunteer who faces threats of violence or harassment because of affiliation with a gender-affirming health services facility. Prohibits a person, business or association from soliciting, selling or trading on the internet or social media personal information or images of providers, employees, volunteers or patients with certain intent. Prohibits certain reports of testosterone or mifepristone prescriptions.
author: Ward (D)

title: California AI Transparency Act
summary: Requires a large online platform to, among other things, related to the provenance of content on the platform, detect whether any provenance data that is compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards-setting body is embedded into or attached to content distributed on the large online platform. Prohibits, beginning on specified date, a GenAI system hosting platform from knowingly making available a GenAI system that does not place disclosure.
author: Wicks (D)

title: Pupil Instruction: High Schools: Computer Science
summary: Establishes the California Computer Science Demonstration Grant Program for specified purposes, including increasing the number of public high schools offering a computer science course to increase pupil access to computer science education and increasing the computer science course access of pupils eligible for free or reduced-priced meals and pupils that are underrepresented in the field of computer science.
author: Berman (D)

title: California Cybersecurity Integration Center: AI
summary: Requires the State Cybersecurity Integration Center to develop, in consultation with the Office of Information Security and the Government Operations Agency, a State AI Cybersecurity Collaboration Playbook to facilitate information sharing across the cyber and artificial intelligence communities and to strengthen collective cyber defenses against emerging threats. Requires the center to review federal requirements, standards, and industry best practices, and to use those resources to inform the playbook.
author: Irwin (D)

title: Budget Act of 2025
summary: Makes appropriations for the support of the government of the State of California and for several public purposes in accordance with the provisions of Section 12 of Article IV of the Constitution of the State of California, relating to the state budget, to take effect immediately, budget bill.
author: Budget and Fiscal Review Cmt

title: Budget Act of 2025
summary: Provides that the Budget Act of 2025 would make appropriations for the support of State government for the specified fiscal year. Amends the Budget Act of 2025 by amending, adding, and repealing items of appropriation and making other changes.
author: Budget and Fiscal Review Cmt

title: Budget Acts of 2022, 2023, and 2024
summary: Provides that the Budget Act of 2022, the Budget Act of 2023, and the Budget Act of 2024 made appropriations for the support of State government for the specified fiscal years. Amends those budget acts by amending, adding, and repealing items of appropriation and making other changes.
author: Budget and Fiscal Review Cmt

title: Artificial Intelligence Technology
topics: Criminal Use; Deepfake; Judicial Use; Private Sector Use
summary: Defines various terms related to artificial intelligence and digital replication and clarifies that false impersonation includes the use of a digital replica with the intent to impersonate another for purposes of these and other criminal provisions. Requires a specified warning to be hyperlinked on any page or screen where the consumer may input a prompt to the technology and included in the terms and conditions for use of the technology.
author: Ashby (D)

title: Workplace Surveillance Tools
status: Pending - Carryover - Assembly Privacy and Consumer Protection Committee
topics: Effect on Labor/Employment; Private Sector Use
summary: Requires an employer to annually provide a notice to the Department of Industrial Relations, in the Labor and Workforce Development Agency, of all the workplace surveillance tools the employer is using in the workplace. Requires the notice to include, among other information, the personal information that will be collected from workers and consumers and whether they will have the option of opting out of the collection of personal information.
author: Smallwood-Cueva (D)

title: Community Colleges: Personnel: Qualifications
summary: Relates to the California Community Colleges. Requires a community college instructor, librarian, counselor, student personnel worker, supervisor, administrator, chief administrative officer, extended opportunity programs and services worker, disabled students programs and services worker, apprenticeship instructor, or supervisor of health to be a person who meets specified minimum qualifications to serve in that position or the alternative qualifications to serve in that position.
author: Cervantes (D)

title: Companion Chatbots
topics: Notification; Private Sector Use; Private Right of Action
summary: Provides that among other things related to making a companion chatbot platform safer for users, if a reasonable person interacting with a companion chatbot would be misled to believe that the person is interacting with a human, require an operator of a companion chatbot platform to issue a clear and conspicuous notification indicating that the companion chatbot is artificially generated and not human.
author: Padilla (D)

title: State Bar of California
topics: Education Use; Judicial Use; Effect on Labor/Employment
summary: Requires the California Lawyers Association or the affiliated 501(c)(3) organization to submit an annual report to the Legislature detailing their use of funds and a statement of compliance with the prohibition on creating, operating, or soliciting members for affinity or royalty programs involving similar products or services.
author: Umberg (D)

title: Fair Online Pricing Act
summary: Provides that the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018 grants to a consumer various rights with respect to personal information that is collected by a business. Provides for the Fair Online Pricing Act. Prohibits, subject to specified exceptions, a price offered to a consumer through the consumer's online device from being generated, in whole or in part, based on certain input data, including the presence or absence of any software on the online device.
author: Wahab (D)

title: California Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025
status: Pending - Carryover - Assembly Third Reading File
summary: Enacts the California Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025. Prohibits person from distributing or making recommendations based on the use of a pricing algorithm to a specified number or more competitors if the person knows or should know that the pricing algorithm processes competitor data. Establishes an affirmative defense to liability under this prohibition for a person who demonstrates by a preponderance of evidence that they exercised reasonable due diligence.
author: Hurtado (D)

title: Data Brokers: Data Collection and Deletion
summary: Requires a data broker to provide additional information to the agency, including whether the data broker collects consumers' names, dates of birth, zip Codes, email addresses, phone numbers, login or account information, various government identification numbers, mobile advertising, connected television, or vehicle identification numbers, citizenship data, union membership status, sexual orientation status, gender identity and gender expression data, and biometric data.
author: Becker (D)

title: Employment: Artificial Intelligence
topics: Government Use; Effect on Labor/Employment; Studies
summary: Requires the Department of General Services to contract with the University of California, Los Angeles Labor Center to conduct a study evaluating the impact of artificial intelligence on worker well being, job quality, job types, different populations, and State revenues. Requires the department, on or before the specified date, to submit a report of the findings of the study to the Legislature. Repeals these provisions upon submission of that report.
author: Smallwood-Cueva (D)

title: Preventing Algorithmic Price Fixing Act: Prohibition
summary: Provides for the Preventing Algorithmic Price Fixing Act. Prohibits a person from selling, licensing, providing, or price-setting algorithm with the intent or reasonable expectation that it be used by a specified number or more competitors in the same market if the person knows or should know that the algorithm processes nonpublic data to set either a price or supply level of a good or service or a rent or occupancy level of rental property. Provides a user of such algorithm an affirmative defense.
author: Wahab (D)

title: Automated Decision Systems
status: Pending - Carryover - Assembly Privacy and Consumer Protection Committee
topics: Government Use; Impact Assessment; Private Sector Use
summary: Requires a developer or a deployer of a high-risk automated decision system to perform an impact assessment before making it publicly available or deploying it. Authorizes the Attorney General or the Civil Rights Department to allow a developer or deployer to cure certain violations. Prohibits an agency from awarding a contract for a high-risk automated decision system unless the person to whom the contract is awarded has certified that the system does not violate, among other civil rights laws, this bill.
author: Padilla (D)

title: State Government: Efficiency of Public Sector
summary: States the intent of the Legislature to enact legislation that would lessen the time, effort, money, and programmatic expertise of local public sector workers in compliance with state reporting and permit processing, as specified.
author: Cabaldon (D)

title: High-risk Artificial Intelligence Systems
summary: Imposes a duty on a covered deployer, defined as a business that deploys a high-risk artificial intelligence system that processes personal information, to protect personal information held by the covered deployer, subject to certain requirements.
author: Becker (D)

title: February 2025 Bar Exam: Audit
topics: Audit; Judicial Use; Effect on Labor/Employment; Studies
summary: Relates to the State Bar Act. Requires the State Auditor to conduct an audit of the specified bar exam and to submit the audit as soon as possible to the Board of Trustees of the State Bar, the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, and to the Assembly and Senate Committees on Judiciary. Requires the State Bar to provide the California State Auditor with the funding necessary to cover the costs of the audit.
author: Umberg (D)

title: Health Care Services: Artificial Intelligence
summary: Specifies that the Department of Public Health is not required to independently inspect, test, or evaluate the functionality of an artificial intelligence system. Requires, beginning January 1, 2027, developers to provide a report identifying compliance efforts with the specified provisions to the department before making an artificial intelligence system commercially or publicly available to a deployer.
author: Weber (D)

title: Housing Rental Terms: Algorithmic Devices
summary: Makes it unlawful for any person to sell, license, or provide to a certain number or more persons a rental pricing algorithm with the intent or reasonable expectation that it be used by a specified number or more persons to set rental terms for residential premises. Makes it unlawful for a person to set or adopt rental terms based on the recommendation of a rental pricing algorithm if the person knows or should know that the rental pricing algorithm processes nonpublic competitor data for certain purposes.
author: Perez S (D)

title: Law Enforcement Agencies: Artificial Intelligence
summary: Requires each law enforcement agency to maintain a policy to require an official report prepared by a law enforcement officer or any member of a law enforcement agency that is generated using artificial intelligence either fully or partially to include specified information, including a disclosure statement and the signature of the law enforcement officer or member of a law enforcement agency who prepared the official report. Requires an agency utilizing artificial intelligence to generate a first draft.
author: Arreguin (D)

title: Artificial Intelligence Models: Large Developers
topics: Cybersecurity; Government Use; Impact Assessment; Private Sector Use; Studies
summary: Enacts the Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act. Provides that the TFAIA would exempt from the California Public Records Act a report of a critical safety incident submitted to the Office of Emergency Services, a report of assessments of catastrophic risk from internet use, and a covered employee report made pursuant to the whistleblower protections.
author: Wiener (D)

title: Electrical Corporations: Data Centers: Report
summary: Provides that existing law authorizes the commission to fix the rates and charges for every public utility and requires that those rates and charges be just and reasonable. Authorizes the Public Utilities Commission to assess the extent to which electrical corporation costs associated with new loads from data centers result in cost shifts to other electrical corporation customers.
author: Padilla (D)

title: Mental Health and Artificial Intelligence
summary: Requires the Secretary of Government Operations to appoint a mental health and artificial intelligence working group that would evaluate certain issues to determine the role of artificial intelligence in mental health settings. Requires the working group to take input from various stakeholder groups, including health organizations and academic institutions, and conduct at least a specified number of public meetings.
author: Padilla (D)

title: California Education and Workforce Development
summary: Relates to the State Career Technical Education Incentive Grant Program. Requires successful applicants to demonstrate a holistic approach to providing career technical education and career pathways. Requires the department to consult with the California Education Interagency Council instead of the chancellor for those purposes.
author: Padilla (D)

title: Privacy: Use of a Person's Name
summary: Provides that a party seeking relief may also seek an injunction or temporary restraining order according to specified procedures. Requires the respondent to comply with the order within 2 business days from the day the order is served, unless otherwise required by the order, if the court grants the applicant a temporary restraining order without notice to the opposing party that requires the respondent to remove, recall, or otherwise cease the publication.
author: Cortese (D)

title: Artificial Intelligence Program: Attorney General
summary: Requires the Attorney General to establish and maintain a specified program to build internal expertise in artificial intelligence, including its applications, risks, regulatory implications, and civil rights impacts. Requires, on or before the specified date, and annually thereafter, the Attorney General to submit a public report to the Legislature describing the program, key developments in artificial intelligence law and policy, and recommendations for additional State oversight or safeguards.
author: McNerney (D)

title: Employment: Automated Decision Systems
topics: Government Use; Effect on Labor/Employment; Notification
summary: Requires an employer to provide a written notice that an automated decision system, for the purpose of making employment-related decisions, not including hiring, is in use at the workplace to all workers that will foreseeably be directly affected by the ADS. Requires an employer to notify a job applicant that the employer utilizes an ADS in hiring decisions, if the employer will use the ADS in making decisions for that position. Prohibits an employer from using an ADS that does certain functions.
author: McNerney (D)

title: Personal Rights: Liability: Social Media Platforms
summary: Provides that existing law prohibits a person from using violence or intimidation to interfere with another person's enjoyment of certain rights or because of certain attributes of that person. Makes a social media platform that violates the provisions of law relating to personal rights through its algorithms that relay content to users or aids, abets, acts in concert, or conspires in violation of those laws, liable for specified civil penalties. Provides that such provisions are severable.
author: Stern (D)

title: Multistakeholder Regulatory Organizations
summary: Provides that existing law requires the Department of Technology to conduct a comprehensive inventory of all high risk automated decision systems that have been proposed for use, development or procurement by, or are being used, developed, or procured by, a State agency. Establishes a process by which the Attorney General designates a private entity as a multistakeholder regulatory organization. Authorizes the Attorney General to establish a fee structure for charging fees to applicants and designated MROs.
author: McNerney (D)

title: Critical Infrastructure: Automated Decision Systems
summary: Provides that existing law requires the Technology Recovery Plan element of the State Administrative Manual to ensure the inclusion of cybersecurity strategy incident response standards. Requires an operator responsible for operating, managing, overseeing, or controlling access to critical infrastructure, that deploys a covered artificial intelligence (AI) system to establish a human oversight mechanism that ensures a human monitors the system's operations in real time.
author: McNerney (D)

title: Public Safety Omnibus
summary: Renames the Prison Industry Authority as the California Correctional Training and Rehabilitation Authority, would rename the Prison Industry Board as the California Correctional Training and Rehabilitation Board, would rename the Prison Industries Revolving Fund as the California Correctional Training and Rehabilitation Revolving Fund, and would require that any reference to the Prison Industry Authority be deemed a reference to the California Correctional Training and Rehabilitation Authority.
author: Public Safety Cmt

title: Public Higher Education: Artificial Intelligence Usage
status: Pending - Carryover - Assembly Higher Education Committee
summary: Encourages the President of the University of California, the Chancellor of the California State University, and the Chancellor of the California Community Colleges to create a workgroup of faculty, staff, and administrators to review the use of artificial intelligence in higher education, and create a report and make public the strategies and best practices for artificial intelligence usage agreed upon by the workgroup.
author: Niello (R)

title: Classified Workers Rights
summary: Urges President Donald J. Trump and the Congress of the United States to approve federal legislation guaranteeing specified rights to classified workers that would, among other things, empower those workers to work in a stable, safe environment and receive livable and competitive wages.
author: Cortese (D)

title: Pricing Coordination Between Landlords
summary: Prohibits a landlord from subscribing to, contracting with, or exchanging any form of consideration in return for the services of a coordinator, prohibits a coordinator from facilitating an agreement among landlords that restricts competition, prohibits two or more landlords from engaging in consciously parallel pricing coordination, provides that a violation is punishable in accordance with the State Antitrust Act of 2023, requires the Division of Housing to develop a public education program.
author: Woodrow (D)

title: Consumer Protections and Artificial Intelligence System
topics: Education Use; Government Use; Notification; Private Sector Use
summary: Concerns implementing consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence systems.
author: Lindstedt (D)

title: Artificial Intelligence Systems
topics: Effect on Labor/Employment; Private Sector Use
summary: Concerns artificial intelligence systems.
author: Weinberg (R)

title: Statewide Government Language Access Assessment
summary: Requires the Department of Personnel, in collaboration with the Office of New Americans, to conduct or contract to conduct a statewide language access assessment, specifies what the assessment must identify, including the needs of principal departments to meet the language access standards, provides that the department may enter into an agreement with a third party entity to conduct all or part of the assessment, appropriates funds to the department for use by the State Equity Office.
author: Velasco (D)

title: Public Safety Protections Artificial Intelligence
topics: Effect on Labor/Employment; Notification; Private Sector Use; Private Right of Action
summary: Concerns public safety protection from the risks of artificial intelligence systems.
author: Rutinel (D)

title: Prohibits Intimate Personal Data Automated Analysis
topics: Criminal Use; Private Sector Use; Responsible Use
summary: Concerns limiting the use of automated analysis of intimate personal data to make inferences that impact a person's financial position.
author: Mabrey (D)

title: Social Media Tools for Minor Users Parents
summary: Concerns tools to protect minor users of social media.
author: Caldwell (R)

title: Detection Components for Wildfire Mitigation
summary: Requires the division of fire prevention and control in the Department of Public Safety to establish public-private agreements with one or more private partners, by which agreements the state may allocate responsibility or risk to one or more private partners to develop and operate wildfire detection components.
author: Daugherty (D)

title: Extend Prohibition on School Facial Recognition
summary: Concerns the limited use of facial recognition services by schools, provides that for a product, device, or software application that allows for analysis of facial features for educational purposes in conjunction with curricula, allows for the analysis of facial features to identify a person who has made a significant threat against a school or the occupants of a school, or to identify a missing student.
author: Daugherty (D)

title: Applying Artificial Intelligence to Fight Wildfire
summary: Concerns the application of artificial intelligence, predicts, prevents, or assists in fighting wildfires, makes an appropriation.
author: Baisley (R)

title: Electronic Discovery in Criminal Cases Task Force
summary: Relates to the creation of the Electronic Discovery in Criminal Cases Task Force, provides that the task force consists of a specified number of task force members, provides that the purpose of the task force is to study the costs and management of electronic discovery in criminal cases.
author: Bridges (D)

title: Data Center Development and Grid Modernization Act
summary: Concerns benefits to facilitate data center development while supporting electric grid infrastructure, creates the State data center development and grid modernization act.
author: Hinrichsen (D)

title: Intimate Digital Depictions Criminal Civil Actions
topics: Child Pornography; Criminal Use; Deepfake; Notification; Private Right of Action
summary: Concerns preventing certain disclosures of intimate depictions, creates a cause of action for nonconsensual disclosure of an intimate digital depiction and adding and amending related provisions in criminal law.
author: Rodriguez (D)

title: Artificial Intelligence Consumer Protections
topics: Government Use; Impact Assessment; Effect on Labor/Employment; Private Sector Use; Responsible Use
summary: Concerns consumer protections in interactions with artificial intelligence systems.
author: Rodriguez (D)

title: Increase Transparency for Algorithmic Systems
topics: Health Use; Housing; Notification; Private Sector Use; Responsible Use
summary: Concerns measures effective no later than June 30, 2026, to increase transparency for algorithmic systems.
author: Rodriguez (D)

title: Tech Neutral Anti Discrimination Clarification Act
topics: Education Use; Housing; Effect on Labor/Employment; Responsible Use
summary: Concerns clarifying anti-discrimination protections in interactions with artificial intelligence systems.
author: Baisley (R)

title: Protections for Users of Social Media
summary: Concerns protections for users of social media, and, in connection therewith, establishing certain requirements for social media companies, provides that general assembly finds that self-regulation by social media companies has not worked, and it is time for the State to step in and put common-sense laws in place to protect its youth, directs social media companies to provide annual data about minors' use of social media platforms, including metrics concerning criminal activity.
author: Frizell (R)

title: Unlawful Dissemination of Intimate Images
summary: Relates to the unlawful dissemination of intimate images that are digitally altered or created through the use of artificial intelligence, criminalizes the nonconsensual creation and dissemination of deep fake pornography.
author: Carpino (R)

title: Task Force to Study Artificial Intelligence
summary: Creates a task force to study artificial intelligence and the State workforce, studies the practicality and use of increased artificial intelligence by the State and automation of the size and scope of the State workforce.
author: Lanoue (R)

title: Study of the Effect of Artificial Intelligence
summary: Requires a study of the effect of artificial intelligence on the trades industry, studies the effect of artificial intelligence on the trades industry.
author: Lanoue (R)

title: Energy and Water Efficiency Requirements
topics: Energy; Private Sector Use; Responsible Use
summary: Concerns energy and water efficiency requirements for artificial intelligence data centers, promotes energy and water consumption efficiency in artificial intelligence data centers.
author: Rosario (D)

title: Health Insurers
summary: Prohibits any health insurer from using artificial intelligence as the primary method to deny health insurance claims.
author: Menapace (D)

title: Artificial Intelligence
summary: Prohibits any health insurer from using artificial intelligence to deny health insurance claims.
author: Chafee (D)

title: Creation and Dissemination of Artificial Intelligence
summary: Establishes a crime prohibiting the creation and dissemination of artificial intelligence generated pornographic images of a person without such persons consent.
author: Canino (R)

title: Use of Artificial Intelligence to Replace Teachers
summary: Prohibits the use of artificial intelligence to replace public school educators in providing instruction to and regular interaction with students.
author: Napoli (D)

title: Health Data
summary: Concerns health data, establishes additional standards governing the ownership, collection, storage and use of health data.
author: Foster (D)

title: Use of Certain Software
summary: Prohibits the use of certain software that uses one or more algorithms to examine data for the purpose of increasing landlord and property manager profits by constraining housing supply and increasing rental rates.
author: Rochelle (D)

title: Pricing Algorithms
summary: Prohibits residential rental property owners from using pricing algorithms and competitors' sensitive data to set rental prices.
author: Rojas (D)

title: Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Synthetic Media
summary: Concerns artificial intelligence, deceptive synthetic media and elections, prohibits distribution of certain deceptive synthetic media within the ninety-day period preceding an election or primary.
author: Joint Government Admin and Elections

title: Residential Rental Property Owners From Using Pricing
summary: Prohibits residential rental property owners from using pricing algorithms and competitors' sensitive data to set rental prices.
author: Joint Housing

title: State Agency Contracts for the Licensing of Software
summary: Concerns state agency contracts for the licensing of software applications, prohibits state agency contracts for the licensing of software applications from limiting a state agency's ability to install the software on the state agency's chosen hardware.
author: Joint Government Admin and Elections

title: Legal Proceedings
summary: Concerns legal proceedings, involves housing matters and the impermissible use of pricing algorithms and competitors' sensitive data to set rental prices.
author: Joint Judiciary

title: Health Insurance and Patient Protection
summary: Concerns health insurance and patient protection, provides that each health carrier shall file a certification with the Insurance Commissioner for the immediately preceding calendar year, certifying that such health carrier completed a review of such health carrier's administrative practices for compliance with the state and federal mental health and substance use disorder benefit reporting requirements.
author: Looney (D)

title: Creation and Dissemination of Intimate Images
summary: Prohibits the creation and dissemination of intimate images generated using artificial intelligence and without consent, prohibits the production and distribution of deepfake intimate images that are generated without the consent of the individual depicted, establish criminal penalties for violations of such prohibition and make civil remedies available for victims.
author: Anwar (D)

title: Artificial Intelligence
summary: Concerns Artificial Intelligence, implements the Governor's budget recommendations, provides that the Chief Data Officer and agency data officers shall identify appropriate data to make available for use by artificial intelligence systems, machine learning and other statistical means of data analysis.
author: Office of the Governor

title: Energy and Water Efficiency Requirements
summary: Concerns energy and water efficiency requirements for artificial intelligence data centers, requires an owner or operator of an artificial intelligence data center to submit a report to the Commissioner of Energy and Environmental Protection.
author: Joint Energy and Technology

title: Unauthorized Dissemination of Intimate Images
summary: Concerns unlawful dissemination of an intimate synthetically created image, provides that unlawful dissemination of an intimate synthetically created image to a person by any means is a class D misdemeanor.
author: Joint Judiciary

title: Artificial Intelligence Protections for Employees
topics: Government Use; Effect on Labor/Employment; Private Sector Use; Responsible Use
summary: Implements artificial intelligence protections for employees, limits the use of electronic monitoring by an employer, establishes various requirements concerning the use of artificial intelligence systems by employers.
author: Joint Labor and Public Employees

title: Artificial Intelligence
summary: Concerns artificial intelligence, provides that the Technology Talent and Innovation Fund Advisory Committee shall partner with public and private institutions of higher education in the state and other training providers to develop programs in the field of artificial intelligence, including, but not limited to, in areas such as prompt engineering, artificial intelligence marketing for small businesses and artificial intelligence for small business operations.
author: Looney (D)

title: Unauthorized Dissemination of Synthetic Intimate Images
summary: Prohibits unauthorized dissemination of certain synthetic images.
author: Somers (R)

title: Unlawful Dissemination of Intimate Images
summary: Concerns unlawful dissemination of intimate images that are digitally altered or created through the use of artificial intelligence, criminalizes unauthorized dissemination of intimate images that are digitally altered or created through the use of artificial intelligence.
author: Hwang (R)

title: Health Carriers and Using Artificial Intelligence
summary: Prohibits health carriers from using artificial intelligence in the evaluation and determination of patient care to safeguard patient access to testing, medications and procedures.
author: Anwar (D)

title: Software Tools and Health Insurance Claims
summary: Prohibits any health insurer from using a software tool, including, but not limited to, artificial intelligence or an algorithm, to automatically downcode or deny a health insurance claim submitted by a health care provider without detailed review by a clinical peer.
author: Looney (D)

title: Employment Practices
summary: Empowers job applicants with crucial information to negotiate salaries and make informed career decisions, encourages businesses to proactively review compensation practices, address unjustified pay disparities, and strengthen their ability to attract and retain top talent, requires that employers include salary or wage range information and a general description of benefits in all postings for job opportunities, and ensures that applicants have access to that information.
author: Ross Levin (D)

title: Artificial Intelligence Commission
summary: Relates to the Artificial Intelligence Commission, adds a high school student to the AI Commission as a nonvoting member, provides that the Chair of the Commission will appoint a student who is, or will be in the next school year, a tenth, eleventh, or twelfth grade student in a public or private school in the State, provides that priority must be given to the selection of an individual who has demonstrated an interest in and commitment to the study of AI.
author: Griffith (D)

title: Large Energy Use Facilities
status: Pending - Carryover - House Natural Resources and Energy Committee
summary: Requires regulated utilities to establish a separate rate for large energy-use facilities that mitigates the risk of costs associated with expanding infrastructure and maintaining reliability in the face of growing demand from being shifted to residential, small business, and other electric customers.
author: Burns (D)

title: Nuclear Energy Feasibility Task Force
summary: Establishes the Delaware Nuclear Energy Feasibility Task Force to examine the feasibility, economic impact, regulatory considerations, energy reliability, and environmental implications of deploying Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) in Delaware.
author: Richardson (R)

title: Stop Discrimination by Algorithms Act of 2023
status: Failed - Adjourned - Business and Economic Development Committee
summary: Prohibits users of algorithmic decision-making from utilizing algorithmic eligibility determinations in a discriminatory manner, requires corresponding notices to individuals whose personal information is used, provides for appropriate means of civil enforcement.
author: White (D)

title: Artificial Intelligence Literacy in Education
status: Pending - Committee Of the Whole Committee
summary: Directs local education agencies to adopt and implement a model AI literacy policy addressing appropriate use and instruction of artificial and generative intelligence by students and staff for educational purposes.
author: Pinto (D)

title: Deepfake Political Advertising Regulation
status: Failed - Adjourned - Executive Administration and Labor Committee
summary: Requires that all candidates, political action committees, political committees, independent expenditure committees and other certain entities that publish, distribute, disseminate, or cause to be published, distributed, or disseminated, to another person in the District, certain campaign materials or political communications that use or contain artificial media created or produced using generative artificial intelligence include a certain disclosure in a certain manner.
author: Allen (D)

title: Agency for Persons with Disabilities
summary: Requires the Agency for Person with Disabilities to provide a list of all qualified organizations located within the region in which the client resides and to post its quarterly reconciliation reports on its website within specified timeframes, requires the agency to participate in transition planning activities and to post the total number of individuals in each priority category on its website, establishes the Statewide Family Care Council.
author: Kincart Jonsson (R)

title: K 12 School Transportation
summary: Revises provisions relating to student transportation requirements and hazardous walking conditions.
author: Alvarez (R)

title: Hurricane Mitigation Grants and Insurers Regulations
summary: Requires Department of Financial Services (DFS) to require that certain mitigation improvements be made as condition of reimbursing homeowner approved for M. Requires an operator, of a companion chatbot to, on or before specified date to do various things with respect to child safety and companion chatbots, including annually perform and document a comprehensive risk assessment to identify any child safety risk, as defined, posed by the design, configuration, and operation of the companion chatbot that assesses, among other things, the likelihood of a covered harm, as defined, occurring to child users.
author: Wicks (D)

title: Tenancy: Digitally Altered Images: Disclosure
summary: Requires a person who includes a digitally altered image, as defined, in an advertisement or other promotional material for the rental of real property to include a disclosure. Requires the unaltered image to be included, unless the image, architectural rendering, or artistic rendering was not originally created through the use of a capture device.
author: Pellerin (D)

title: Worker Data: Prohibitions: Artificial Intelligence
topics: Private Sector Use; Private Right of Action
summary: Prohibits an employer from using a workers personal information to train an artificial intelligence system to replicate, automate, or replace a workers job, and prohibits an employer from selling, disclosing, or otherwise providing access to a workers personal information to a third party for the purpose of training an AI system to replicate, automate, or replace a job. Authorizes a worker who suffered a violation to bring a civil action for damages, injunctive relief, punitive damages, and attorneys fees.
author: Ward (D)

title: Pupil Instruction: Digital Wellness
summary: Requires the State Department of Education, on or before January 1, 2028, to develop a plan to expand digital wellness instruction in California public schools.
author: Hoover (R)

title: Elementary and secondary education
summary: Establishes a system of public elementary and secondary education in this state. Requires school districts, county offices of education, and charter schools employ personnel to provide instruction to and services for pupils in kindergarten and grades 1 to 12, inclusive, at school sites throughout the state. Defines, for purposes of the Education Code, both a public school employee and a contractor providing services in a public school to mean a natural person.
author: Muratsuchi (D)

title: Social Media Platforms: Artificial Intelligence
summary: Enacts the Digital Choice Act. Requires a social media company or a person that makes an artificial intelligence model available to a third party for use, modification, copying, or combination with other software, defined as a deployer, to allow a consumer to request a copy of the consumer's personal information, contextual data, and social graph and would require the social media company or deployer to respond to that request within five business days.
author: Lowenthal (D)

title: Postsecondary Education: Sexual Harassment
summary: Defines additional terms for purposes of the act, including, among other terms, digitized sexually explicit material, sextortion, technology-facilitated sexual harassment, and affirmative consent. Revises the definitions of sexual harassment and sexual exploitation and make conforming changes.
author: Bauer-Kahan (D)

title: Lubricants Waste: Packaging: Producer Responsibility
summary: Creates a producer responsibility program for lubricants waste that is not covered by the Oil Recycling Enhancement Act and packaging associated with lubricant products. Requires a producer responsibility organization to provide a convenient collection and management system. Requires the charge be set at an amount that is adequate to cover CalRecycle's and DTSC's actual and reasonable costs of administering and enforcing the program.
author: Rodriguez Mi (D)

title: Pupil Safety: Nonconsensual Artificial Intimate Images
summary: Requires the State Department of Education to conduct a study on nonconsensual artificial intimate images involving pupils in the specified grades. Requires the study to include, among other things, a summary of the resources for schools regarding nonconsensual artificial intimate images and the effects of nonconsensual artificial intimate images on pupils.
author: Lackey (R)

title: Pupil Instruction: Computer Science: Content Standards
summary: Requires the Instructional Quality Commission, on or before July 31, 2019, to consider developing and recommending to the state board computer science content standards for kindergarten and grades 1 to 12, inclusive, pursuant to recommendations developed by a group of computer science experts, as specified. Requires the commission, when the computer science content standards are next revised after January 1, 2027, to consider incorporating cybersecurity skills, as defined, into those standards.
author: Irwin (D)

title: Electricity: Data Centers
summary: Requires, as part of a new or existing proceeding, the commission to require each electrical corporation to file a transmission and distribution service tariff and a generation service tariff for participating customers, as defined, that meet certain requirements, as specified. Requires, on or before January 1, 2028, each community choice aggregator or electric service provider to adopt a tariff for generation service for data centers consistent with certain requirements.
author: Zbur (D)

title: Public Postsecondary Education: Artificial Intelligence
summary: Establishes the State Community Colleges, under the administration of the Board of Governors of the State Community Colleges, the California State University, under the administration of the Trustees of the California State University, and the University of California, under the administration of the Regents of the University of California as the 3 segments of public postsecondary education in the state.
author: Fong M (D)

title: Income Tax: Credits: Commercial Production
summary: Excludes any commercial that is created entirely by generative artificial intelligence, as specified, or that utilizes generative artificial intelligence or autonomous vehicles in a manner that replaces the job functions customarily performed by a human worker in the production.
author: Elhawary (D)

title: State Agencies or Departments: Public Communications
status: Failed - Adjourned - Senate Privacy, Digital Technologies, and Consumer Protection Committee
summary: Requires that disclaimer when a state agency or department uses GenAI to directly communicate with the public and would define directly communicate to mean to use GenAI, instead of a natural person, to communicate directly with a specific member of the public or to communicate a general public announcement.
author: Ta (R)

title: Downcoding Medical Claims
summary: Provides that existing law sets forth requirements by which a health care service plan or health insurer reimburses a provider for health care services. Requires a determination to downcode a claim, which is the unilateral alteration by a payer of the service or procedure code submitted on a claim resulting in a lower payment, to include a documented review of the clinical information supporting the billed service.
author: Patel (D)

title: State Government: Benefits
topics: Government Use; Private Sector Use; Taxes
summary: Prohibits a business entity that is directly invested in, owns, operates, or manages a private detention facility, or that contracts with the federal government for immigration enforcement purposes, from receiving any State provided grant or loan. Prohibits a disqualified taxpayer from receiving any tax credits. Establishes the Due Process for All Fund and requires the Controller to transfer to the Fund the amount of tax collected that is attributable to business entities being made ineligible for credits.
author: Ortega (D)

title: Data Centers: Water Use Disclosures
summary: Prohibits a city, county, or city and county from approving a discretionary or ministerial permit or other entitlement that would result in the construction, or an expansion that increases the maximum peak water use, of a data center unless specified conditions are satisfied, including, among others, that the applicant provides the city, county, or city and county prescribed information.
author: Papan (D)

title: Artificial Intelligence: Education and Workforce
status: Failed - Adjourned - Assembly Higher Education Committee
topics: Education Use; Education/Training; Effect on Labor/Employment
summary: Enacts the Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Development Act to accomplish specified goals, including, among others, empowering and supporting community college instructors in using and deploying artificial intelligence responsibly in administrative and classroom settings, and strengthening the States AI and technology workforce pipeline by upskilling and educating all workers so they can benefit from AI.
author: Ahrens (D)

title: Community Colleges: Artificial Intelligence
topics: Education/Training; Effect on Labor/Employment; Notification; Private Sector Use; Studies
summary: Establishes the State Community Colleges, administered by the Board of Governors of the State Community Colleges, as one of the segments of public postsecondary education in the state. Requires the board to appoint a chief executive officer, known as the Chancellor of the State Community Colleges. Establishes community college districts throughout the state, under the administration of community college district governing boards. Authorizes these districts to provide instruction at the community college.
author: Bauer-Kahan (D)

title: Report: Labor Force Impact: Artificial Intelligence
summary: Establishes the State Artificial Intelligence Worker Impact Data Assessment Project and establishes the State Artificial Intelligence Worker Impact Data Assessment Project Advisory Panel in the Employment Development Department. Requires the Employment Development Department (EDD), in consultation with the advisory panel, to perform an assessment of data sources and collection methods regarding the use and impact of advanced artificial intelligence systems on the labor force.
author: Schiavo (D)

title: Surveillance Pricing
status: Failed - Adjourned - Assembly Unfinished Business - Concurrence in Senate Amendments
summary: Provides that its provisions do not limit or impair any consumer right or remedy available under any other state or federal law.
author: Ward (D)

title: Health Care Services: Artificial Intelligence
topics: Health Use; Notification; Private Sector Use
summary: Declares it is the policy of the state that a worker providing direct patient care be free to use their professional judgment to make assessments and decisions within their scope of practice as appropriate for their patients. Prohibits an employer from retaliating or discriminating against a worker providing patient care.
author: Ortega (D)

title: Crimes: Prostitution
summary: Requires a person who commits prostitution with intent to receive compensation, money, or anything of value from another person to, for a first or second violation of those provisions, be offered a diversion program pursuant to specified provisions.
author: Schultz (D)

title: Small Business Advocate: Artificial Intelligence
summary: Enacts the AI for Main Street Act, which would require the Small Business Advocate to provide assistance to small businesses in evaluating artificial intelligence concerning operations, including by providing information, guidance, and training, developing training materials, and conducting outreach.
author: Hoover (R)

title: Water Resources: Data Centers
summary: Requires a person who owns or operates a data center, prior to applying to a city or a county for an initial business license, equivalent instrument, or permit, to provide its water supplier, under penalty of perjury, a good faith estimate of the expected water use, the anticipated source of water, and the data centers projected water use volume for the maximum day, maximum month, and average year.
author: Papan (D)

title: State Contracts: Report: Modern Foundation Models
summary: Requires the Department of Industrial Relations, in consultation with the Department of Technology, to convene a Foundation Model Labor and Procurement Working Group consisting of 9 members, assess labor practices underlying the development of modern foundation models and associated artificial intelligence systems and develop recommendations regarding whether and how the state should incorporate labor standards into procurement decisions for foundation models and associated artificial intelligence systems.
author: Lee (D)

title: Public Employees: Notice: Artificial Intelligence
summary: Requires certain state and local public employers to provide written notice to a recognized employee organization at least 45 days before taking an action to develop, purchase, or require the use of GenAI to perform a service that is within the scope of work of the job classification represented by the recognized employee organization.
author: Petrie-Norris (D)

title: State AI Transparency Act: System Provenance Data
summary: Revises the duties and prohibitions applicable to a large online platform relating to artificial intelligence, including the requirement for allowing a user to inspect system provenance data. Specifies that these provisions do not require a large online platform to take any action with respect to provenance data, system provenance data, or digital signatures that are not compliant with widely adopted specifications issued by an established standards-setting body.
author: Wicks (D)

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence: Training Data
summary: Requires a developer of a generative artificial intelligence model to make available on its internet website a mechanism allowing a rights owner to request information about the developer's use of the rights owner's covered materials that would allow the rights owner to provide the developer with, among other things, registration, preregistration, or index numbers and fingerprints for one or more covered materials. Makes technical changes.
author: Bauer-Kahan (D)

title: Elections: Deceptive Media In Advertisements
summary: Prohibits the distribution of materially deceptive content that is material to a voter's electoral decisions or to public confidence in an election's process or outcome. Specifies that the prohibition applies within the 30 days before an election in California with regard to candidates for any federal, state, or local elected office and elected officials and, with regard to elections officials and voting machines and related equipment, beginning 30 days before an election through 38 days after the election.
author: Pellerin (D)

title: Reproductive Health Emergency Preparedness Program
summary: Establishes the Reproductive Health Emergency Preparedness Program for the purpose of expanding and improving access to reproductive and sexual health care in emergency departments across the State. Requires the Department of Health Care Access and Information to award the grants and administer the RHEPP. Requires the department to establish minimum standards, funding schedules, and procedures for awarding grants. Limits the permissible uses of grant funds.
author: Krell (D)

title: Elections: Deceptive Audio or Visual Media
summary: Authorizes a candidate for elective office whose voice or likeness appears in audio or visual media distributed in violation of this section to seek injunctive or other equitable relief prohibiting the distribution of the deceptive audio or visual media. Authorizes a candidate whose voice or likeness appears in the deceptive audio or visual media to bring an action for general or special damages against the person, committee, or other entity that distributed the media.
author: Berman (D)

title: California AI Transparency Act
summary: Delays CATA's operation with respect to a GenAI system that is designed to primarily function as assistive technology, as defined. Prohibits a covered provider from falsely representing that a GenAI system is designed to primarily function as assistive technology and would punish a covered provider who makes such a false representation with a certain civil action.
author: Becker (D)

title: Energy: Utility Infrastructure AI Safety
summary: Requires the commission, on or before January 1, 2028, to adopt standards for an electrical or gas corporation's use of artificial intelligence models. Requires the commission to direct an electrical or gas corporation to file a plan that demonstrates the corporation's compliance with those standards.
author: McNerney (D)

title: Automated License Plate Recognition Systems
status: Failed - Adjourned - Assembly Third Reading File
summary: Provides that public agency does not include a transportation agency, a public transit operator, department of transportation, public works department, or campus transportation agency, as specified, a public agency or contracted parking operator when engaging in specified activities in a parking facility, a state agency operating specified parking facilities, or the State Air Resources Board.
author: Cervantes (D)

title: Crimes: Minors
summary: Makes any adult person who recruits, induces, coerces, or persuades a minor to commit an illegal act against another minor, or to solicit physical harm, sexual conduct, or images of an intimate body part, from another minor, or who utilizes a minor as a conduit of communication to facilitate any such acts guilty of a crime punishable either as a misdemeanor or a felony. Repeals certain provision.
author: Strickland (R)

title: False Advertising: Synthetic Digital Performers
summary: Makes it an unlawful advertising practice for a person to create and cause to be published in an advertising medium an advertisement that prominently includes a synthetic performer without a clear and conspicuous disclosure that the advertisement includes a synthetic performer. Prohibits an advertising medium from transmitting, distributing, displaying, airing, or otherwise making available an advertisement containing a synthetic performer if a court of competent jurisdiction has issued an order.
author: Ashby (D)

title: Covered Provider: Goods and Services: Self Preferencing
status: Failed - Adjourned - Senate Privacy, Digital Technologies, and Consumer Protection Committee
summary: Prohibits a covered provider from preferencing its own products, services, or lines of business over those of another business user, including manipulating the order of search results or rankings to favor the products or services of the covered provider. Prohibits a covered provider from restricting interoperability or data portability, including restricting a business user or consumer from obtaining a copy of their data in a useful and portable format. Relates to actions for civil or criminal penalties.
author: Wiener (D)

title: Budget Act of 2026
summary: Makes appropriations for the support of the government of the State of California and for several public purposes in accordance with the provisions of Section 12 of Article iv of the Constitution of the State of California, relating to the state budget, to take effect immediately.
author: Laird (D)

title: Large Home Improvement Retailers: Immigration
summary: Requires retail store doing business in this state, as defined, to provide the Attorney General with copies of specified documentation related to immigration enforcement activity, as defined, that occurs on the large retail store's premises, including copies of any video footage, upon receipt of an administrative subpoena.
author: Perez S (D)

title: Agentic Artificial Intelligence
topics: Cybersecurity; Energy; Private Sector Use; Studies
summary: Requires the Department of Technology to annually submit to certain legislative committees a report regarding a specified required comprehensive inventory of all high-risk automated decision systems that have been, or are being, used, developed, or procured by a state agency. Defines high-risk automated decision system. Requires the comprehensive inventory in the report to include agentic artificial intelligence that has been, or is being, used, developed, or procured by a state agency.
author: Cabaldon (D)

title: Budget Act of 2026
summary: Amends the Budget Act of 2026 by amending, adding, and repealing items of appropriation and making other changes.
author: Laird (D)

title: Digital Replicas
summary: Provides that existing law creates a civil cause of action against any person who knowingly uses the name, voice, signature, photograph, or likeness of another person, without their consent, for specified purposes. Clarifies that a voice or likeness includes a digital replica. Clarifies that false impersonation includes the use of a digital replica with the intent to impersonate another.
author: Ashby (D)

title: Companion Chatbots: Childrens Safety
summary: Requires a person who owns, maintains, or controls a software application to request age bracket data sent by a real-time secure application programming interface or operating system with respect to a particular user from an operating system provider or a covered application store when the application is downloaded and launched.
author: Padilla (D)

title: Budget Acts of 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025
summary: Relates to the Budget Act of 2022, the Budget Act of 2023, the Budget Act of 2024, and the Budget Act of 2025 made appropriations for the support of state government for the 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 fiscal years, respectively. Amends those budget acts by amending, adding, and repealing items of appropriation and making other changes.
author: Laird (D)

title: Pupil Instruction: Preventative Health Instruction
summary: Provides for the Ready to Learn, Ready for Health Act. Requires, when the Health Education Framework for California Public Schools is next revised on or after the specified date, the Instructional Quality Commission to consider including information on evidence based preventative health instruction, including information on nutrition, food literacy, sleep, movement, stress management, and digital balance in an integrated manner that discusses these key health factors and the interrelationship between them.
author: Strickland (R)

title: Budget Acts of 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025
summary: Amends specified budget acts by amending, adding, and repealing items of appropriation and making other changes.
author: Laird (D)

title: Digital Dignity Act
summary: Enacts the Digital Dignity Act. Provides that subject to specified liability a person who, by distributing content with actual knowledge that the content includes a digital replica, is found guilty of violating a criminal provision for which false impersonation of another is a required element or is found liable in a civil action arising from the use or portrayal through a digital replica.
author: Becker (D)

title: Advertisement Claims: Health Related Consumer Products
topics: Deepfake; Health Use; Notification; Private Sector Use
summary: Requires a person who creates or causes to be created an advertisement that includes a digital replica or synthetic performer depicted as a health care provider to promote the sale of a health-related consumer product or service to include a clear and conspicuous disclosure that the health care provider depicted in the advertisement was generated or substantially altered by artificial intelligence or that no human health care provider is depicted.
author: Gonzalez (D)

title: Artificial Intelligence: Transparency and Governance
summary: Prohibits a person from knowingly using artificial intelligence to falsely represent that a natural person appeared before, submitted information to, or otherwise engaged with a governmental agency. Requires local agencies, for the purpose of ensuring public access to the meetings of public bodies and the writings of public officials and agencies, to comply with a statutory enactment that amends or enacts laws relating to public records or open meetings.
author: Cabaldon (D)

title: Data Centers: Rate Structures
summary: Requires the commission to assess opportunities for rate structures to ensure data centers pay a reasonable share of their costs associated with transmission and distribution needs, ensure that data centers pay for their proportionate share of load increases and procurements needed to reliably serve their loads while maintaining consistency with the applicable integrated resource planning requirements, and alleviate cost pressures on residential ratepayers.
author: McNerney (D)

title: Violence Prevention Pupil Wellness, and School Safety
summary: Requires the department, in consultation with the Office of Emergency Services, to establish and administer the Violence Prevention, Pupil Wellness, and School Safety Grant Program to, upon appropriation by the Legislature, award grants to eligible school districts, county offices of education, or charter schools for evidence-based violence prevention, pupil wellness, and public safety initiatives, as specified.
author: Hurtado (D)

title: Nonconsensual Intimate Image Clearinghouse
summary: Requires the Department of Justice to establish the Nonconsensual Intimate Image Clearinghouse to allow individuals who were exploited in the State to submit a request for the removal of nonconsensual intimate images from covered platforms. Requires the department to transmit verified identifiers of images to covered platforms and require those platforms to remove verified matches within 48 hours of receipt and to prevent the images from being uploaded again.
author: Grove (R)

title: State Agencies: Automated Decision Systems
summary: Imposes certain restrictions on the use of an automated decision system by a state agency to confer services, defined as, among other things, the issuance of professional licenses and provision of public benefits.
author: Cabaldon (D)

title: Education Finance: Education Omnibus Trailer Bill
summary: Require the Superintendent to provide notice of an action to reclassify a certification to the governing board of the county office of education. Provides that if a county office of education receives a negative certification, the bill would require, instead of authorizing, the Superintendent, or their designee, to take specified actions that are necessary to ensure that the county office of education meets its financial obligations.
author: Budget and Fiscal Review Cmt

title: Crimes: Sexual Exploitation of a Child
summary: Makes a person guilty of a misdemeanor or a felony if the person knowingly does any of the specified actions, or downloads, streams, or accesses through electronic or digital media the above-described sexual conduct, knowing that the matter depicts a person under 18 years of age engaged in an act of sexual conduct, except as specified. Broadens definition of sexual exploitation to include any digitally altered or artificial-intelligence-generated matter.
author: Rubio (D)

title: Elections: Vote By Mail Ballots
summary: Makes it a misdemeanor for any person having charge of a vote by mail ballot to interfere, as defined, with a ballot's delivery to a voter. Makes it a felony for a person with authority to direct one or more persons subject to their supervision or authority to interfere with a ballot's return to the local elections official or delivery to a voter. Specifies that the State Constitution requires the state to reimburse local agencies and school districts for certain costs mandated by the state.
author: Wahab (D)

title: Companion Chatbots
summary: Require a companion chatbot operator to take the above actions when it has constructive knowledge that a user is a minor. Requires an operator to prevent its companion chatbot from producing or facilitating the exchange of any sexually explicit material or proposing sexually explicit conduct.
author: Padilla (D)

title: Insurance Information and Privacy Protection Act
summary: Provides that on and after July 1, 2028, this bill would revise the Insurance Information and Privacy Protection Act to establish new standards for the processing and sharing of consumers' personal information by insurance licensees, surplus line insurers, reinsurers, and third-party service providers. Authorizes processing or sharing of a consumer's personal information for specified purposes, including sharing in connection with an insurance transaction.
author: Limon (D)

title: Employment: Artificial Intelligence
topics: Government Use; Effect on Labor/Employment; Studies
summary: Requires the Department of General Services to contract with the University of California, Los Angeles Labor Center to conduct a study evaluating the impact of artificial intelligence on worker well being, job quality, job types, different populations, and State revenues. Requires the department, on or before the specified date, to submit a report of the findings of the study to the Legislature. Repeals these provisions upon submission of that report.
author: Smallwood-Cueva (D)

title: Property Tax: Welfare Exemption: Detention Facilities
topics: Government Use; Impact Assessment; Private Sector Use
summary: Specifies that for the purposes of the welfare exemption provisions above, property used exclusively for religious, hospital, scientific, or charitable purposes shall not include property, or any portion thereof, operated as a detention facility.
author: Padilla (D)

title: Local Agencies: Automated Decision Systems
summary: Imposes certain restrictions on the use of an automated decision system by a local agency to confer supportive services, permits, or licenses. Includes a prohibition on using an output from the system as the sole basis for an adverse eligibility or benefit determination affecting a natural person, except as specified. Requires the local agency to verify the accuracy of the system's outputs and to promote nondiscrimination in its use.
author: Cabaldon (D)

title: California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018
summary: Provides that the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018 grants to a consumer various rights with respect to personal information that is collected by a business including the right to delete personal information. Revises that part of the definition of publicly available by removing the condition that the business have a reasonable basis to believe the information is lawfully made available.
author: Wahab (D)

title: High-risk Artificial Intelligence Systems
summary: Imposes a duty on a covered deployer, defined as a business that deploys a high-risk artificial intelligence system that processes personal information, to protect personal information held by the covered deployer, subject to certain requirements.
author: Becker (D)

title: Health Care Services: Artificial Intelligence
summary: Requires developers and deployers, as defined, of an artificial intelligence system that produces a prediction, classification, recommendation, evaluation, or analysis that aids decisionmaking related to diagnosis or treatment, known as a clinical decision support system, to make reasonable efforts to identify clinical decision support systems developed for use by deployers that are known or have a reasonably foreseeable risk for biased impacts resulting from deployment of the system in health programs.
author: Weber (D)

title: Attorneys, Arbitrators, Judicial Officers
summary: Prohibits an attorney from delegating the practice of law to generative artificial intelligence. Requires an attorney who uses generative artificial intelligence to assist in the practice of law to, among other things, not enter confidential, personal identifying, and other nonpublic information into a generative artificial intelligence system, as specified. Requires an attorney to take reasonable steps to verify the accuracy of generative artificial intelligence outputs.
author: Umberg (D)

title: Mental Health and Artificial Intelligence
summary: Requires the Secretary of Government Operations to appoint a mental health and artificial intelligence working group that would evaluate certain issues to determine the role of artificial intelligence in mental health settings. Requires the working group to take input from various stakeholder groups, including health organizations and academic institutions, and conduct at least a specified number of public meetings.
author: Padilla (D)

title: Golden Gate Bridge, Highway and Transportation District
summary: Authorizes the district to accept contributions and loans from this state and the United States for the purpose of financing capital improvements or modifications related to seismic safety on the Golden Gate Bridge.
author: Wiener (D)

title: Artificial Intelligence Program: Attorney General
summary: Requires the Attorney General to establish and maintain a specified program to build internal expertise in artificial intelligence, including its applications, risks, regulatory implications, and civil rights impacts. Requires, on or before the specified date, and annually thereafter, the Attorney General to submit a public report to the Legislature describing the program, key developments in artificial intelligence law and policy, and recommendations for additional State oversight or safeguards.
author: McNerney (D)

title: Access To Connected Vehicle Service
summary: Amends Vehicle Code provisions governing connected vehicle service, with a focus on the timeline for requiring vehicles to notify occupants when connected vehicle location access is enabled. Modifies definitions of key terms, including connected vehicle service and vehicle, and establishes a phased operative schedule for compliance by model year.
author: Cabaldon (D)

title: Independent Verification Organizations
topics: Government Use; Oversight/Governance; Private Sector Use
summary: Requires, on or before specified date, the Department of Technology, within the Government Operations Agency, to conduct, in coordination with other interagency bodies as it deems appropriate, a comprehensive inventory of all high-risk automated decision systems that have been proposed for use, development, or procurement by, or are being used, developed, or procured by, any state agency. Requires the department to annually submit a report of that comprehensive inventory.
author: McNerney (D)

title: Critical Infrastructure: Automated Decision Systems
summary: Provides that existing law requires the Technology Recovery Plan element of the State Administrative Manual to ensure the inclusion of cybersecurity strategy incident response standards. Requires an operator responsible for operating, managing, overseeing, or controlling access to critical infrastructure, that deploys a covered artificial intelligence (AI) system to establish a human oversight mechanism that ensures a human monitors the system's operations in real time.
author: McNerney (D)

title: Toys: Companion Chatbots
summary: Prohibits the manufacture, sale, exchange, possession with intent to sell or exchange, and exposition or offer for sale or exchange to a retailer a toy, as defined, that includes a companion chatbot and would make violations of the bill subject to the same civil liability as violations of the provisions applicable to operators of companion chatbots in the specified described paragraph.
author: Padilla (D)

title: Technology Innovation and Ratepayer Protection Act
summary: Relates to California Technology Innovation and Ratepayer Protection Act. Requires the Public Utilities Commission, on or before July 1, 2027, to establish separate tariffs for the interconnection of the participating customer facilities and the provision of transmission, distribution, and optional generation services to participating customers.
author: Padilla (D)

title: California Environmental Quality Act: Environmental
summary: Defines data center for the purposes of California Environmental Quality Act and prohibit the application of categorical exemption to a project for the development and operation of a data center, as specified. Provides that by increasing the duties of a lead agency in relation to the environmental review of a data center project, the bill would impose a state-mandated local program. Authorizes the Governor to certify a data center project that is certified by the lead agency to meet specified conditions.
author: Padilla (D)

title: Mental Health Professionals: Artificial Intelligence
summary: Regulates the use of artificial intelligence in connection with providing or facilitating psychotherapy services, as defined. Authorizes an individual, corporation, or entity that provides or facilitates psychotherapy services to use artificial intelligence tools or systems only to assist in providing administrative or supplementary support in psychotherapy services. Prohibits an individual, corporation, or entity from using artificial intelligence to record or transcribe psychotherapeutic communications.
author: Padilla (D)

title: Civil Actions: Housing Development Projects
summary: Provides that existing law provides that in a civil action brought by a plaintiff to challenge a housing development project that meets or exceeds the requirements for low- or moderate-income housing, a defendant may seek an order requiring the plaintiff to furnish an undertaking as security for costs and damages that may be incurred by the defendant if the bringing of the action would result in preventing or delaying the project. Makes these provisions applicable to a student housing development.
author: Ashby (D)

title: California State University: Faculty Employees
summary: Provides that existing law requires certain community college employees to be a person who meets specified minimum qualifications. Requires the instructor of record for a course of instruction to be a person who meets the rule provided by the Trustees of the California State University to serve as a faculty employee teaching credit instruction or noncredit instruction.
author: Cervantes (D)

title: Employment: Automated Decision Systems
summary: Prohibit an employer, as defined, from using an Automated Decision Systems (ADS) to perform certain functions and would limit the purposes for and way in which an ADS may be used. Provides that when an employer primarily uses an ADS to make a disciplinary or termination decision, authorize an employee to request, and require an employer to provide, a description of the employee's own data primarily used by an ADS to make a disciplinary or termination decision, as specified.
author: McNerney (D)

title: Employment: Technological Displacement: Notice
topics: Effect on Labor/Employment; Notification; Private Sector Use
summary: Revises the Cal/WARN Act to also require an employer giving notice of a mass layoff, relocation, or termination caused in whole or in substantial part by an artificial intelligence (AI) system or other automated technology replacing or automating employment positions to include certain information in the notice, including the job functions performed by workers that will be automated by AI or other automated technology.
author: Reyes (D)

title: Public Higher Education: Artificial Intelligence Usage
summary: Encourages the President of the University of California, the Chancellor of the California State University, and the Chancellor of the California Community Colleges to create a workgroup of faculty, staff, and administrators to review the use of artificial intelligence in higher education and create a public report on the strategies and best practices for artificial intelligence usage agreed upon by the workgroup within one year following formation of the workgroup.
author: Niello (R)

title: Data Center and Utility Modernization
